task.title: Run your site from the admin console
task.shortdesc: Staff readers run the docs site in the browser at /admin: who can read it, which repository it is built from, readers and organizations, sign-in, the GitHub connection and the web editor. No server access or environment variables needed.

context.p: Only signed-in staff readers can open the console. Anyone else gets a 404; visitors who are not signed in are sent to the sign-in page first. Staff readers see an Admin link next to their name on every docs page.

The console works without JavaScript. Every change is a form protected by a token tied to your session, is refused from other sites, and is written to the audit log as staff:your email. A change applies at once on every server, without a restart.

step.cmd: Become the first staff reader with a one-time setup link.

info.p: The first time, nobody is staff yet. Whoever operates the server mints a setup link, which works once, for 30 minutes, and only while no staff reader exists:
info.codeblock: opend-server admin-link # on Railway: run it in the web service's shell # or, with the admin token: curl -X POST "$PUBLIC_URL/admin/api/setup-links" -H "authorization: Bearer $OPEND_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"minutes":30}'
info.p: Open the link, enter your email address and name, and you are signed in as a staff reader of the staff organization (or your existing reader is made staff). Use the address you will sign in with from then on, with GitHub or your company account. On a managed site, the hosting provider makes you staff when the site is created.

stepresult.p: The console's Overview opens, with what is left to set up.

step.cmd: Connect GitHub on the GitHub page.

info.p: Self-hosted sites create their own GitHub App in a few clicks (). Managed sites install the provider's app with Connect GitHub.

step.cmd: Choose the docs repository on the Docs source page.

info.p: Pick it from the repositories the GitHub App can access, or give a public repository's https:// clone URL. Set the branches and tags that publish (such as main, v*) and the folder that holds opend.config.yaml. Build now queues a build of every matching branch and tag; Rebuild now does it again later. Choosing another repository keeps the site's access settings and readers.

step.cmd: Decide who can read the site on the Site & access page.

info.p: Private or Public, and for a public site the products, features and release anonymous visitors see, chosen from those the published release declares in opend.config.yaml. See . The site title comes from the repository and is shown read-only.

step.cmd: Add organizations and readers on the People page.

info.p: An organization's products, features and release decide what its readers see. Readers sign in with an account whose verified email is the one you give. Make teammates staff here; you cannot remove your own staff role, yourself or your own organization.

step.cmd: Choose how readers sign in on the Sign-in page.

info.p: Sign in with GitHub comes with the connected GitHub App and can be turned off. Company sign-in (OIDC) takes the issuer URL, client id and client secret from your identity provider; register $PUBLIC_URL/auth/callback there as the redirect URI. Demo readers can be turned off where the server allows them; they never appear in production.

step.cmd: Set up the web editor on the Editor page.

info.p: Give the editor's address to turn on Edit this page links, choose whether View source on GitHub links show, and add authors who sign in with company sign-in. The editor service itself needs only DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET, EDITOR_PUBLIC_URL and PUBLIC_URL; see .

result.p: Settings set by environment variables are shown as Set by environment and cannot be changed in the console; see . Secrets you enter (client secrets) are stored encrypted and never shown again: the console only says whether one is set.
